thread:
elena: Heads up — after yesterday's kernel selector patch + the scheduler tweak (increasing max_wait_ms for some classes) we're seeing p99 tail-rise on a few customer workloads. baseline p99 ~310ms -> 520ms on the worst shard. Anyone else seeing this?

max: yeah saw that on canary. p50 unchanged, p95 up a bit, p99 spike ~+70%-80% for prompt-heavy short requests. Throughput (tokens/s) increased ~8% for that shard.

tom: interesting — do we have per-kernel timings? my hunch is microbatch shapes causing different kernel path (fused vs fallback).

elena: i attached quick profile excerpt below (from perf-trace sample of the offending node):

```
2026-03-10T14:02:12Z shard-11 sample:
requests: 312 over 60s
config: max_batch_tokens=4096, max_wait_ms=12, microbatch_target=64
kernel-path: fused_attention.v2 (fast)  -> sometimes fallback to "attention_matmul_slow"
KV/cache hit ratio: 0.74 -> 0.67 during spikes
p50  40ms
p95 180ms
p99 520ms

trace snippet:
  allocate_kv_cache  : 3.6ms
  kv_lookup(hit)      : 0.9ms
  matmul_attn_fused   : 12.4ms (when chosen)
  matmul_attn_slow    : 78.1ms (fallback)
  dispatch_overhead   : 5.8ms
```

sara: KV hit dip stands out. If prefix caching or coalescing is less effective we push different seq-length distributions into kernel picker and hit cold path. Did we change any cache sharding or TTL?

max: no TTL change. But increasing max_wait_ms to 12 raised average wait window so more requests got coalesced across slightly different seq lengths — that can create microbatches with more variance in seq-len, making the kernel selector pick a more conservative (safer) kernel to avoid OOM, which is slower.

jonathan: put another way: higher max_wait -> bigger/longer microbatches -> higher chance the longest sequence in microbatch triggers non-optimized kernel. throughput up (more tokens), but tail latency suffers. Classic latency vs throughput tradeoff.

elena: exactly. Quick experiment results from canary:
- max_wait_ms=8, max_batch_tokens=4096: p99=330ms, tokens/s=185k
- max_wait_ms=12, max_batch_tokens=4096: p99=520ms, tokens/s=200k
- max_wait_ms=6, max_batch_tokens=3072: p99=310ms, tokens/s=160k

so lowering wait helps p99 but reduces throughput. We need a middle ground or smarter batching rules.

tom: could we bias coalescing by seq-length? i.e. prefer coalescing requests with similar lengths, or limit batch length variance when kernel fallback is expensive. Implementation idea: when forming microbatch, compute max_len and median_len and reject adding a request if (max_len - median_len) > threshold.

max: that'd be a scheduler heuristic. cheap to add and only applied when kernel_picker predicts fallback delta > X ms. kernel_picker already exposes predicted_latency delta for candidate kernels — we can gate coalescing by that signal.

sara: also worth checking KV cache alignment: if coalescing groups different prefixes, KV hit ratio can drop. We could add a soft affinity key (e.g., session prefix hash) to prefer grouping same-customer requests where caching matters.

jonathan: good point. For privacy/tenancy we already keep tenant-id; using that to bias coalescing is safe and should improve KV hit ratio for many workloads.

infra-bot: deploy pipeline update: branch "microwait/kernel-heuristics" built and pushed to staging (image: infra/microwait:2026-03-11-rc1).

elena: plan proposal:
1) short-term: roll back the global max_wait_ms bump for the affected class to 8ms for prod-hot shards (restore p99 baseline).
2) medium: land scheduler heuristic: seq-length variance gating + tenant affinity for coalescing, plus gate on kernel_picker.predicted_delta > 20ms to avoid bad fallbacks.
3) long-term: collect training data for a learned coalescer that predicts latency cost vs throughput benefit per candidate add.

max: I ran a quick sim on historical traces with seq-variance gating (threshold=20 tokens) + tenant affinity; result: p99 reduced ~35% relative to the high-wait config and throughput drop only ~3%. KV hit ratio recovered from 0.67 -> 0.72 in the sim.

tom: can you drop the sim outputs in the thread? quick numbers we can show SRE/PM.

max: pasted csv summary below (very rough):

```
config, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, tokens_s, kv_hit
high_wait (12/4096), 42, 180, 520, 200000, 0.67
low_wait (8/4096), 40, 170, 330, 185000, 0.74
gated (12/4096 + gating), 41, 175, 340, 194000, 0.72
```

sara: nice. Action items?

elena: I'll open a small rollback PR to adjust max_wait_ms for the class nodes and add a followup RFC for the gating heuristic with perf sims attached. max will prototype the scheduler gate; tom will add kernel_picker hook to expose predicted_delta per kernel decision. jonathan will notify affected customer-facing teams.

jonathan: ping me when rollback is live and when we have sim artifacts. I'll draft a short note for CS.

infra-bot: deploy started for rollback config to prod-hot shard group at 2026-03-11T02:20:00Z. CI: green.

elena: thanks everyone — let's keep this thread for tests / sim uploads. If someone hits a different shard with similar symptoms please post profile + kv-hit time series.

max: will post prototype branch link later today.

tom: FYI — also spotted a small regression in kernel cold-start handshake that could amplify fallback cost; adding to my TODOs.

sara: thumbs up :thumbsup:

elena: closing loop: rollback rolled out, monitoring shows p99 back to ~340ms, tokens/s down ~5% on those shards. Leaving the gating RFC as next step.
